questions.question: Describe the coastal plain of South Africa and name two cities found on it.
questions.expected_answer: The coastal plain is a strip of low, mostly flat land along the coast, much of it near sea level. It is wide and flat in Maputaland in north-east KwaZulu-Natal and narrower and hillier elsewhere. It has a mild climate. Cities on it include Durban, Richards Bay, East London, Gqeberha and Cape Town.

questions.question: What is the Great Escarpment? Describe where it runs and name two parts of it.
questions.expected_answer: The Great Escarpment is a long line of steep mountains and cliffs that separates the low coastal areas from the high plateau. It curves around the country, roughly parallel to the coast, from Limpopo through Mpumalanga, along the KwaZulu-Natal and Lesotho border, through the Eastern Cape and north-west into the Northern Cape and Namibia. Parts include the Drakensberg, the Stormberg, the Sneeuberg, the Nuweveld and the Roggeveld.

questions.question: Describe the plateau and name two regions and two cities on it.
questions.expected_answer: The plateau is the high, fairly flat land inside the escarpment, covering most of the country, mostly more than one thousand metres high, highest in the east and sloping to the west. Regions include the Highveld, the Great Karoo and the Kalahari. Cities include Johannesburg, Pretoria, Bloemfontein and Kimberley.
